Stated explicitly because "priority queue" ordinarily implies preemption and here it must not — the clause a naive implementation violates first. **§3.3** the reservation is enforced at load, not by reviewer memory (a binding claiming an unbuilt class is refused). **§3.4** *new design finding*: **shed-batch is partially self-defeating**. Class 3's premise is "CPU is stressed, move batch work to the GPU", but the lane is not a pure GPU resource — its host threads sit on q3's physical cores, so shedding consumes CPU in the region most likely contended under CPU stress. Bounded (8 host threads, not a 48-thread quarter) but concentrated, and shared with frontdoor 8380 / worker_general 8382+8072 / ingest 8485 / vision_escalation 8087 / architect_general 8083. Net benefit is (GPU gained − q3 CPU lost), **never measured**; the Step-4 recert already produces the pairwise inputs. Recorded so that "don't build class 3" can be a measurement outcome rather than the reversal of a shipped feature. Four tests link prose to code (class order vs spec section, unbuilt set = classes 3–4, reserved flags absent from the registry, no preemption path in the lease module).

**P2-5a — shed-trade measurement DESIGNED** ✅ 2026-07-28 (research **`d5f5942f`**, `docs/design/p2-5a-shed-trade-measurement-spec.md`). **Design only — nothing run.** Two design decisions changed what gets measured: (1) **the metric is `task_rate`, not t/s** — §3.4's "GPU t/s gained − q3 CPU t/s lost" phrasing is not commensurable (gemma4-26B-A4B vs a 27B dense: different tokens), and `P-SPEED-OBJ` already settled the axis as task_rate with t/s demoted to host-health telemetry; my own §3.4 framing is corrected in the spec rather than inherited. (2) **the net is measured DIRECTLY**, as a paired whole-system comparison on one frozen corpus in one wall window — reconstructing it from two separately-measured halves inherits both CV≈9.1% noise terms and measures the halves under conditions that never co-occur, which is the entire phenomenon. Four arms: A0 CPU-only under stress · **A1 lane resident but IDLE** (isolates the residency tax — the control most likely skipped, and the one separating "shedding is bad" from "the lane's mere presence is bad") · A2 shed active (**A2−A0 is the answer**) · A3 GPU with CPU quiesced (exposes the GPU-side contention tax). Shed fraction **swept, not assumed** — the optimum may be interior since the residency tax is paid once while CPU displacement grows with *f*, so a single badly-chosen *f* yields a false negative. Controls: order-randomised arms, stress as a declared operating point at two levels, live-affinity verification, `drop_caches`+NUMA re-warm for the ~27 GiB tenant load, host threads fixed at 8 (SMT contention is non-linear and varying it invalidates the ceiling table), acquired q3+GPU claims, eval path only. **Pre-registered**: n≥10, MDE published with the result not after seeing it, e-process never single-trial, and **the null result is pre-registered as informative** so "no detectable trade" is a decision (don't build) rather than something re-litigated as "needs more data" once the feature exists. Crucially the measurement **does not require building class 3** — the split is harness-driven via eval-path fan-out, so a negative result is a decision, not a feature reversal.

**P2-5b — `P-SHED-1` RATIFIED by the operator** ✅ 2026-07-28 (research **`cc6e2c92`**). No existing protocol covered a **cross-device contention trade** (P-BENCH-2 = CPU multi-instance aggregate, P-BENCH-3 = batched slot decode, P-GPU-1 = GPU throughput; none covers *work moved between devices where the mover consumes the resource it is relieving*). Operator ratified the design; a pre-validated ratification command is being packaged for the operator to execute against `MEASUREMENT.md`. **Registration is a human-only path — this session did not and will not touch that file**; ratifying a design and amending a trust boundary are two different acts. Gate G4 in the spec is cleared; no hardware gate moved.

**P2-5d (NEW) — the two decision-rule inputs are UNRESOLVED; recommendations recorded as PROPOSALS, not decisions.** They do not block the measurement, they block turning it into a verdict. (1) **Complexity threshold** — proposed: build only if net ≥ **+10%** of A0 total (below that it is not reliably observable *in production* at CV≈9.1%, and a benefit you cannot see once deployed cannot be operated or defended), AND the gain holds at **both** stress levels rather than one knife-edge point, AND the time-weighted benefit is material. (2) **Stress levels** — proposed: keep the 1.0×/0.5×-saturating bracket but **define saturation operationally** (the knee where CPU task_rate stops rising, located by a calibration sweep that is part of the run — a stress level asserted rather than located makes every arm's "under stress" label unfalsifiable), and add 0.75× **only if the sign flips**, since in that case the crossover *is* class 3's admission trigger. Spec §10 carries a banner that these must not be cited as decided.

**P2-5e (NEW, discovered while proposing the threshold; BLOCKED on P1-3)** — **the stress duty cycle is measured nowhere.** The decision is not only "is the net positive under stress" but "how much of production wall time is under qualifying stress": class 3 is dormant otherwise, so expected benefit is `net_gain × duty_cycle`. A +15% gain during stress occurring 3% of the time is ~0.5% overall, bought with a permanent admission class. Proposed as the third threshold condition (≥15%), and it is the **cheapest** of the three — a small duty cycle closes class 3 without spending the multi-hour window at all. **But it is not runnable now**: verified 2026-07-28 that AutoPilot is **not running** (no process; last journal activity `2026-07-27T08:23:07Z`) because its resume is gated on the E8 signature (P1-3 → P0-1). AutoPilot is the representative production load generator, so measuring duty cycle against a quiesced host would sample the pause and return a near-zero value that would **wrongly close class 3 on an artifact**. Run it over a representative window after P1-3, first among the three conditions.

**P2-5c (NEW, blocked)** — RUN the P2-5a measurement. **Gated, and not merely procedurally:** (G1) `q3` is HELD by `bench-e8-quality` (`e8-v5-r2-cadencefix-20260728T160917Z`, re-verified 2026-07-28T17:0xZ) and the lane's host threads need exactly that region — reclaim is drain-at-boundary, never forced; (G2) host-health tier — uptime measured 4d3h so P-BENCH-1's ≤1wk tier applies today, lapsing ~2026-07-31; scheduled post-reboot regardless, which satisfies it by construction. **Do not squeeze into the pre-07-31 window** — multi-hour campaign, window belongs to E8/E5; (G3) lane activation Steps 0–7, operator-gated, requires G1 first — **G1 precedes G3**; (G4) P2-5b ratification; (G5) operator run grant + quiet window; (G6) acquired q3 + GPU claims.

**P2-5f (NEW, POST-REBOOT ONLY — do not start early)** — **measure the stress duty cycle, and only after AutoPilot has resumed and run representatively.** The dependency chain is invisible from any single link and must be stated explicitly: **P0-1 (E8 signature) → AutoPilot resume (P1-3) → stress duty cycle measurable → complexity threshold settable → P2-5 decision rule executable.** `P-SHED-1` was ratified by the operator 2026-07-28 (epyc-root **`aa0af6e0`**, `MEASUREMENT.md`), but its decision rule's top row — "gain exceeds the operator's complexity threshold" — is still **UNDEFINED**. As ratified, that row does not self-execute: a marginal positive `net_gain` from P2-5c still needs an operator number before it can gate anything. The threshold cannot honestly be set on `net_gain` alone — expected benefit is `net_gain × duty_cycle` (P2-5e), and a large gain during rare stress does not justify a permanent admission class plus flag plus telemetry surface plus failure mode. **The duty cycle is measured nowhere, and measuring it now would be a trap**, which is the point worth preserving here: AutoPilot is the representative production load generator and is currently DOWN (no process; last journal activity `2026-07-27T08:23:07Z`; resume gated on the E8 signature, P0-1 → P1-3), independently re-verified 2026-07-28 by the coordinator. Sampling duty cycle against a quiesced host returns a near-zero value and would **wrongly close class 3 (shed batch) on a measurement artifact**, not a finding. Duty cycle must therefore be measured only **after** AutoPilot has resumed and been running representatively — i.e. post-reboot, post-E8-signature — not against a cold restart. **Open sub-question, not to be pre-answered here:** what "representatively" needs to mean — a stated observation window long enough to cover AutoPilot's natural stress cadence, not an instantaneous sample; the window length is undetermined and should be set by whoever picks this up post-reboot, informed by however much of a duty-cycle history AutoPilot's journal has accumulated by then. Cross-reference: this item elaborates **P2-5e** (the coordinator's own threshold question, corrected in-place after checking AutoPilot's real state rather than assuming it was running) and is what turns **P2-5c**'s eventual `net_gain` measurement into an executable verdict rather than a number waiting on a still-undefined constant. **A future session must not pick this up before the reboot and the E8 signature land — doing so repeats the exact artifact mistake this item exists to prevent.**

**P2-5g (NEW 2026-07-29, from fable-auditor's read-only P-SHED-1 review; POST-REBOOT, operator-granted)** — **dissolve the class-3 premise instead of measuring it: mint a finer region.** The sharpest point in the review is that the lane needs **8 SMT threads (184-191, siblings of physical 88-95 — spec §4.5 already fixes the lane at exactly this shape)** while `region-lock` granularity forces claiming **all of q3 (24 physical + 24 SMT)**. The all-or-nothing displacement of the 122B architect is therefore a **claim-granularity artifact, not a physical impossibility**: the architect runs 96 *physical* cores, the lane wants 8 *SMT siblings*, and their true contention is SMT-sibling execution pressure on 88-95 under a BW-bound workload — plausibly small. Path: measure the architect×lane contention **pair** (`contention_matrix.yaml` is per-role-pair by design) and, if the tax on the 122B is acceptable, mint `q3-smt-hi = 184-191` so the lane claims 8 threads and **the 122B never goes down at all**. That converts class 3 from *displace-the-largest-model* into an **8-thread co-residency certification** — cheaper to measure, cheaper to operate — and moots the two spec defects below. Fabric axioms hold: the sub-region is still a real flock; the matrix entry is policy-data.

**P2-5h (NEW 2026-07-29, same review) — two defects in the P-SHED-1 spec as written, to fix before any class-3 run.** (a) **Corpus scope:** §2 pins the corpus as the `worker_general`-class batch corpus, but `architect_general` serves a different duty and **zero corpus tasks invoke it** — so in lane-resident arms the 122B is necessarily absent (topology exclusion via the q3 claim) yet `task_rate` registers **no loss**. The metric prices displaced worker-class capacity on a quarter, not the loss of the entire architect service. (b) **Arm contradiction:** §2 line 70 pins the q3 co-tenant set *including* `architect_general:8083`, while §3 arms A1-A3 *hold* the q3 claim — under claim exclusivity those cannot coexist, so architect-down is a **hidden arm difference** in both directions: an unpriced missing service, and a confound (stopping the architect frees its 69GB mlock interleave=all footprint, changing memory pressure on all four nodes; §4.4 covers lane load, not co-tenant teardown), which pollutes the A1−A0 residency-tax diagnostic. Fix: **pin the architect state per arm explicitly** (resident-idle vs stopped is a declared input, not an emergent consequence of the claim), and either add the architect-duty-unavailability × its own duty-cycle loss term (P2-5e logic applied to the displaced tenant) or put architect-class tasks in the corpus. *Reviewer verdict: the spec measures the right quantity on a workload surface that structurally cannot see this displacement.* ✅ 2026-07-29 — research `5e7a1564` changes the frozen corpus to role-stratified `worker_general` + non-sheddable `architect_general` duties, keeps unavailable forced-target rows as zero completions, and makes every arm's q3 lifecycle/memory state explicit. A later device-local/carve topology is a separately declared arm, never a silent exception.

**P2-5i (NEW 2026-07-29, same review) — the 72t/3-quadrant 122B number does not exist; do not quote a bound as a result.** For BW-bound decode, 96t→72t is **sublinear**, so the naive −25% is a *ceiling on the thread term*, not an estimate. The dominant unknowns are layout: `interleave=all` striped mlock'd pages across all four nodes and **mlock'd pages do not migrate**, so a 72t/3-quadrant run either keeps ~1/4 of accesses cross-quadrant on node 3 or needs a **reload** under a 3-node policy (a different arm with a different memory shape) — and the whole point of the exercise is a GPU tenant hammering node-3 bandwidth simultaneously. Placement sensitivity here is historically extreme (**+184% from wiring alone**: Probe B 2026-05-04, 2×48t cross-NUMA 4.3 t/s/instance vs 1×96t 12.19). Reviewer's plausible band is **−10% to −40%** vs 12.19 t/s and they declined to narrow it without data. If the operator wants the number: canonical 122B recipe per P-SPEED, arms = {96t baseline replicate, 72t taskset 0-71 pages-as-loaded, 72t reloaded interleave=0-2} × {lane absent, lane active at pinned shape}, n≥3, order-randomised — **each memory-policy arm needs a model reload (mlock), so this is a multi-hour operator-granted campaign with reload ownership honoured; post-reboot queue, never pre-E8.**

**P2-5j (NEW 2026-07-29, from fable-auditor's design package; run BEFORE any q3 carve)** — **sweep host-thread placement INCLUDING device-local candidates; the threads may not belong on q3 at all.** The MI210 is node-1-attached, and the only placements ever compared were 184-191 vs 88-95 — **both inside q3, both cross-node**. Device-local candidates (node-1 SMT, e.g. within 120-143 / 136-143 over Q0B) were **never tried**, so the current placement is measured-best only among two shapes. If device-local wins, **the entire q3 entanglement dissolves** — the carve happens on Q0B instead — and there is **untested upside**: the lane may get *faster*, which changes the whole trade arithmetic. Cost: any host-thread move invalidates the measured serving-shape lineage and forces re-deriving the ceiling table — but that re-derivation **folds into P2-5c arms**, where the lane is under measurement anyway, making it near-free at the right moment. **Sequencing: do not carve q3 before this runs.** What crossing actually costs, decomposed and unmeasured: doorbell/launch MMIO hops (ns against µs launch overhead — likely negligible); pinned-buffer DMA locality (`hipHostMalloc` pages land by first-touch, so scattered threads scatter staging buffers); and the most plausible penalty, **cache-line ping-pong on the submission/polling state the 8 host threads share** when spread across nodes. Scattered placement is **not disqualified by physics** — the existence proof is today's
